quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #15
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: If two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, what should happen?

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.
Drivers must use hand signals to communicate with each other.
One driver should proceed without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, vehicles should go in the order they arrive. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.

questions.question: You want to turn at an intersection but you are not in the proper lane. What should you do?

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Turn on your signal and turn from your current lane.
Drive to the next intersection and make your turn there.
Safely change lanes and back up to return to the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the next intersection and make your turn there.
questions.explanation: Never make sudden turns. If you are not in the correct lane to turn, drive to the next intersection and turn from the proper lane.

questions.question: Where are stop lines painted?

options.text: On curves and hills.
Next to churches and schools.
At intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.
On freeway on-ramps.

questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.
questions.explanation: Stop lines are solid white lines painted across traffic lanes at intersections and pedestrian crosswalks. They show drivers exactly where to stop.

questions.question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle approaching, what must you do?

options.text: Slow down until it passes you.
Move to the right side of the road and stop.
Signal the emergency vehicle to pass you.
Move to the right lane and continue driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Always give the right-of-way to emergency vehicles with flashing lights or sirens. Move to the right side of the road and stop. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first before stopping on the right side.

questions.question: What should you do when entering a roadway from a private road?

options.text: Honk your horn to warn other cars.
Stop with part of your car on the roadway to alert drivers.
Drive out quickly to merge smoothly with traffic.
Yield to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway.
questions.explanation: When entering a roadway from a driveway or private road, you must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and all traffic on the roadway.

questions.question: You are waiting to turn left at a multi-lane intersection and cannot see around oncoming traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up when the first lane clears.
Wait until you can see all the lanes you need to cross.
Wait for an oncoming driver to wave you across.
Move into each lane as oncoming traffic clears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see all the lanes you need to cross.
questions.explanation: Never start a left turn until you can see that all lanes you need to cross are clear and it is safe to turn.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Trucks under 18,000 lbs. are allowed.
Hill ahead.
Truck stop ahead.
No trucks allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hill ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that there is a steep hill ahead.

questions.question: On which traffic signal do you have the right-of-way to turn left?

options.text: A solid green light
A flashing yellow light
A green arrow pointing left
A flashing red light

questions.correctAnswerText: A green arrow pointing left
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you may turn in the direction the arrow points. Oncoming traffic must stop for you.

questions.question: Where should your car be positioned when making a right turn?

options.text: Near the center of the street.
Close to the left side of the street.
Close to the right side of the street.
Past the center of the intersection when you start to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close to the right side of the street.
questions.explanation: Before making a right turn, position your car as far to the right as possible. Do not cross other lanes to make any turn.

questions.question: Which statement about passing is true?

options.text: Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes to pass and check for oncoming traffic.
Check your mirrors and look over your left shoulder to see your blind spot when passing.
Wait until you see both headlights of the car you passed in your rearview mirror before moving back to your lane.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When passing, signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to see your blind spot. Wait until you see both headlights of the other car in your rearview mirror before returning to your lane.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect a vehicle's stopping distance?

options.text: Your reaction time.
The time of day.
The condition of your brakes.
The condition and type of your tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: The time of day.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on your reaction time, weather, visibility, vehicle weight, brake condition, tire condition and type, road conditions, and speed.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow light mean?

options.text: Merging traffic.
Proceed with caution.
Pedestrian crossing.
Come to a full stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light tells you to drive carefully.

questions.question: How long do you have to title a vehicle after buying it?

options.text: 30 days.
Six months.
One week.
One year.

questions.correctAnswerText: 30 days.
questions.explanation: You must apply for a title within 30 days of buying a vehicle. If you wait longer, you will have to pay a penalty.

questions.question: Why is night driving harder than day driving?

options.text: Cars overheat faster at night.
You cannot see as far or as clearly.
It rains more often at night.
You meet more motorcycles at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as far or as clearly.
questions.explanation: At night, you can see less of the road. Always use your headlights. Drive slowly enough to stop within the distance you can see.

questions.question: What lane space are motorcycles entitled to use?

options.text: The bicycle lane.
The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.
Half the width of a lane.
The width of the sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have the right to use the same full lane width as all other vehicles.

questions.question: A traffic light turns yellow as you approach an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to cross before it turns red.
Brake hard to stop right away.
Get ready to stop in the middle of the intersection.
Get ready to stop before you reach the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get ready to stop before you reach the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the light will soon turn red. Be prepared to stop before the intersection if it is safe.

questions.question: What safety restraints work best in a crash?

options.text: Only a lap and shoulder belt.
Only an airbag.
A lap/shoulder belt and an airbag together.
No safety restraints.

questions.correctAnswerText: A lap/shoulder belt and an airbag together.
questions.explanation: Safety belts greatly improve your chance of surviving a crash and avoiding serious injury. Airbags work best when used with safety belts. Always wear both.

questions.question: At night, when another vehicle approaches from the opposite direction, your headlights should be set to:

options.text: High beam.
Low beam.
Off, using only parking lights.
Either high or low beam.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam.
questions.explanation: Do not use high beam headlights when another vehicle is coming toward you. Switch to low beam to keep everyone safe.

questions.question: You see flashing signals at a railroad crossing. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and look for a train.
Slow down and look for a train.
Look for a train, then speed up.
Do what the car ahead of you does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and look for a train.
questions.explanation: Stop at least 15 feet from the nearest rail when you see flashing signals. Watch for other warning signs like lowered crossing gates or an approaching train.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Left turn yield on green.
One-way.
Cattle crossing.
Two-way left turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Left turn yield on green.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers turning left at a green light to let oncoming traffic pass first. You can complete your turn when it is safe.

questions.question: When two drivers reach an open intersection at the same time, who goes first?

options.text: The driver on the right.
The driver on the left.
One driver can go without stopping.
One driver should honk to show they are giving up their right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right.
questions.explanation: When you arrive at an open intersection at the same time as a vehicle to your right, let that vehicle go first. You can proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Do not enter.
No parking.
No U-turn.
No left turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means U-turns are not allowed at this location.

questions.question: You are driving in the right lane and want to move to the left lane. What should you do?

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for traffic behind you.
Look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot.
Check your side mirror and turn on your signal.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to make sure the lane is clear. Always signal before you change lanes.

questions.question: Your car breaks down in a snowstorm. What should you do?

options.text: Leave the car and walk for help.
Lie down in the car and sleep.
Walk into the road to get other drivers' attention.
Stay in your car where rescuers can find you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car where rescuers can find you.
questions.explanation: Stay in your car when stranded in a snowstorm. You are easier to find in your vehicle. Walking around in a snowstorm is dangerous.

questions.question: When can you go through a stop sign intersection that has no stop line or crosswalk?

options.text: After slowing down to check for cross traffic.
After coming to a complete stop and making sure it is safe.
After stopping at least 20 feet before the intersection.
After slowing to 10 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: After coming to a complete stop and making sure it is safe.
questions.explanation: Stop completely at a stop sign before entering the intersection. When there is no stop line or crosswalk, stop before entering and go when it is safe.
